Dispersion and centroid gap along a path of informativeness

Source: R/algebra-path.R
profile_path.Rd

Keeps the centered logits of a reliability profile fixed and moves its informativeness \(I\), as a change of the between-site standard deviation does when the sampling variances stay fixed. Returns the dispersion, the mean reliability and their second-order terms at each point of the path.

Usage

profile_path(x, I = NULL, n = 201)

Arguments

x

Site reliabilities, a numeric vector of numbers strictly between 0 and 1, or an object of class reliability_profile, reliability_posterior, reliability_draws or reliability_design.

I

Values of the informativeness at which to evaluate the path, a numeric vector of numbers strictly between 0 and 1. By default n equally spaced values.

n

Number of points of the default path, an integer of at least 2.

Value

A data frame with one row for each value of I and the columns

  • I and logit_I.

  • sigma_tau, for an object.

  • H, mean and gap: the dispersion, the mean reliability and the mean reliability minus I.

  • H_leading, gap_leading, H_bound and gap_bound: the second-order terms and the bounds on the remainders, as in local_terms().

Details

Write \(m\) for the logit of \(I\) and \(\Delta_j\) for the centered logits of the profile. Along the path \(\Delta_j\) stay fixed and \(m\) moves, and Proposition 2 of Lee (2026) gives \(\partial H / \partial m = \bar S - I\). So the dispersion rises from 0 while the mean reliability is above \(I\), falls back to 0 after it, and is largest where the gap changes sign.

For an object, the path also gives the between-site standard deviation at each point, \(\sigma_\tau = \{\mathrm{GM}(v)\, I/(1-I)\}^{1/2}\), where \(\mathrm{GM}(v)\) is the geometric mean of the sampling variances. For reliabilities alone the scale is unknown, and that column is absent.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

S <- site_reliability(se = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30), sigma_tau = 0.2)
path <- profile_path(S, n = 9)
path[, c("I", "H", "gap")]
#>     I          H           gap
#> 1 0.1 0.03020018  2.291741e-02
#> 2 0.2 0.05165415  2.834731e-02
#> 3 0.3 0.06605218  2.359490e-02
#> 4 0.4 0.07435859  1.310160e-02
#> 5 0.5 0.07707534 -1.387779e-17
#> 6 0.6 0.07435859 -1.310160e-02
#> 7 0.7 0.06605218 -2.359490e-02
#> 8 0.8 0.05165415 -2.834731e-02
#> 9 0.9 0.03020018 -2.291741e-02
